title: Ownership and ideology

blocks.heading: Ownership and ideology
blocks.text: Capitalism, socialism, mixed economies and communism concern productive ownership and coordination in differing ways; fascism also concerns authoritarian political ideology. Economic and political classifications are separate. Private enterprise can coexist with public services and regulation.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Capitalism
blocks.text: Capitalism emphasises private ownership of productive resources and market allocation. Regulation and public activity can still exist; the label does not imply no state role.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Socialism
blocks.text: Socialism emphasises social ownership or control and collective provision or distribution aims, in varied forms. It is not a single institutional arrangement or a synonym for any public service.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Mixed economy
blocks.text: A mixed economy combines private and public economic activity and different roles for markets and public decisions. The balance varies; a state-owned provider alongside private producers distinguishes it from an exclusively private arrangement.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Communism
blocks.text: Communism as an economic ideal involves common ownership of productive resources and a classless society. Historically labelled communist states have generally used extensive state ownership and planning; the ideal and actual institutions should be distinguished.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Fascism
blocks.text: Fascism is an authoritarian ultranationalist ideology emphasising concentrated leadership, suppression of opposition and subordinating individuals to the state or nation. It is not merely another word for government intervention or a mixed economy.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Apply the distinction
blocks.text: Explain why private shops alongside a state-owned water provider indicate a mixed arrangement rather than exclusively private production. Private and public enterprises coexist. Test ownership across the productive activities, rather than assuming markets or private shops exclude a public role.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated
